correctness.rationale: Every dominating set meeting only one K_n layer is exactly that entire layer, valid for k>=1. A set meeting both layers has uniquely determined four column counts (c,x,y,d), and outside-neighbor bounds c+x+1_{y>0}<=k and c+y+1_{x>0}<=k. The multinomial sum therefore counts every labelled set. For 1<=k<n, at least 2(n-k) vertices are selected in a mixed-layer set, with equality exactly for k omitted entire columns; comparing the two pure layers yields the stated tie and binomial minima. k=0 and k=n boundary proofs are correct. Fresh independent literal-neighborhood enumeration checked full coefficient vectors for all n=2..6 and k=0..n (25 cases), separately from the repository verifier; it proves only these finite checks, not universality.
